t: You're looking at the tomb of Decimus Burton, in Kensington and Chelsea. Burton was one of the foremost English architects and landscapers of the nineteenth century, a leading figure in Greek Revival, Roman Revival and Regency styles. He was a founding fellow and vice-president of the Royal Institute of British Architects, and from 1840 architect to the Royal Botanic Society. He also designed the Athenaeum Club, whose clubhouse was built by the company of his father, James Burton, the pre-eminent Georgian London property developer. This is where he is commemorated.
